newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gesamtmetall reaffirms commitment to sick pay cut.
newsitem.headline: Gesamtmetall reaffirms commitment to sick pay cut.

text.p: Werner Stumpfe, president of the Gesamtmetall federation of German engineering employers, on Thursday reaffirmed his commitment to a law aimed at cutting sick pay allowances from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.
Speaking before talks in Frankfurt with the IG Metall trade union, Stumpfe told journalists: "I couldn't imagine that the unions could offer so much that we would move away from this point."
Stumpfe added that the sick-pay cut was backed up by legislation and as a result should be implemented.

Stumpfe this week was forced to back down on an earlier recommendation that engineering companies should implement the sick-pay cuts immediately. The about-turn followed last week's mass protests by car workers.
